<pre>
cd ~/claude
gh repo clone terrenceb-atlnz/device-testing     # or: git clone git@github.com:terrenceb-atlnz/device-testing.git
</pre>
''First time only: clone into <code>~/claude/</code> in your lab home, because the testboxes run the tools from <code>~/claude/device-testing/</code>. Then follow the repository's <code>README.md</code> one-time setup; its memory-link step matters.''

''How to run a list of test cases on lab hardware with Claude Code's <code>/test-mode</code> skill, and how to turn the results into the logs you attach in Zephyr with <code>/create-logs</code>. Owner: Terrence Beach. Last updated: 6 October 2026. Checked on that date against the <code>test-mode</code>, <code>create-logs</code>, <code>orient-dt</code> and <code>wrap-dt</code> skills, the <code>bench-runner</code> agent, the sentinel kit, <code>bench_probe.py</code>, <code>logged-output.md</code>, <code>STANDING-ORDERS.md</code>, <code>tools/README.md</code> and <code>platforms/IE520.md</code> in the <code>device-testing</code> repository.''

'''<code>/test-mode</code>''' runs a list of test cases on '''any testbox you name''' as one supervised campaign:
* First it asks you about the box: which testbox, which consoles, the PDU, and any constraints.
* It checks that nobody else is using those consoles.
* It measures the bench using the facts you gave it, then works out which cases the bench can run and what blocks the rest.
* It runs the cases the bench can run. For each one it keeps a working log, saves each device's config, and adds the case to a running '''results list'''.
* When the campaign is done you review the results, and then run '''<code>/create-logs</code>''' to build the final output you upload: one <code>.log</code> plus the <code>.cfg</code> files per case.
A watchdog (the ''sentinel'') keeps the run moving and passes messages between you and the tester while it works.

It is part of the [[Ask-ck]] tooling: Ask-CK's Test Composer turns a test case into a <code>.setup</code> + script pair, and <code>/test-mode</code> is how those scripts, and the device-testing campaign cases, get run on hardware.

Throughout, '''the Test Engineer''' means you: whoever invokes the skill. Nothing assumes a particular person, testbox or product. In this page <code><TB></code> is your testbox and <code><FAMILY></code> is the DUT's product family; '''tb470''' and '''IE520''' appear only as marked examples.

__TOC__

== At a glance ==

{| class="wikitable"
! Question !! Answer
|-
| What does it do? || Takes a list of case IDs or titles and sorts them into groups. It checks the bench can run each one, runs the cases it can, and keeps a results list with one verdict per case.
|-
| Which bench? || '''Any testbox you name''' at the start, on '''only the consoles you list'''. Every other console on the box is left alone.
|-
| How many Claude sessions? || '''One.''' The session you type into becomes the sentinel. It starts the tester as a background sub-agent (<code>bench-runner</code>), one per group of cases.
|-
| Will it ask me questions? || Yes, at the start: testbox, consoles, PDU, session constraints, and whether this is a multi-hour run. After triage it asks one more: proceed now, or reconfigure the bench first? After that it asks only when something is genuinely yours to decide. That includes any disagreement between what you said and what the bench or the records show.
|-
| Will it change what I told it? || '''No.''' Your answers are recorded word for word and never overwritten. If the bench or a record disagrees with one, it asks you which is right.
|-
| What if someone else is on the box? || It checks ''before'' it opens any console. If anything is holding your consoles, or could be, it stops and tells you what it found. It never displaces anyone.
|-
| Can it change device config? || Yes, within a test: config, <code>write</code>, reloads and DUT power-cycles that a case needs, on your consoles and your PDU outlets only. It then restores what it changed. Bench-level changes (recabling, applying a new <code>.setup</code>, root on the testbox, licences) stay with you.
|-
| Who decides the verdict? || The tester grades each case. You review the results list and can re-grade any case, at any time until the final logs are made.
|-
| When are the final logs written? || '''Only when you run <code>/create-logs</code>''', after reviewing. Nothing writes them automatically: not <code>/test-mode</code>, not <code>/wrap-dt</code>.
|-
| Where does the output go? || A folder per case: <code><TB>/<FAMILY>/<group>-<STAMP>/<id>/</code> in the <code>device-testing</code> repository. See [[#Where everything is written]].
|-
| Does it upload anything? || '''No.''' You attach each case's <code>.log</code> and <code>.cfg</code> files to the case in Zephyr (Jira) yourself.
|-
| Does it push to GitHub? || No. It commits. Company permissions deny <code>git push</code> to Claude every time; you push.
|-
| How do I resume after a crash? || <code>/test-mode --resume</code>. The queue file and per-case commits are the resume point.
|}

== Before you start ==

# '''Start Claude Code in the repository root''', <code>claude/device-testing/</code> in the lab home. The harness picks which memories a session loads by its launch directory, so a session started anywhere else loads the wrong memories or none. First time on a new dev host: the repository's <code>README.md</code> gives the one-time setup (clone path, memory link, SSH).
# '''Have the answers ready''' for the setup questions (next section): the testbox, your consoles, the PDU's IP and outlets, and anything special about this session.
# '''For a run of more than an hour, start it inside <code>tmux</code>''' (see [[#Running long campaigns: use tmux]]).
# '''SSH from the dev host needs the keyring agent.''' Tool shells do not inherit it, so the tools set <code>SSH_AUTH_SOCK=/run/user/$(id -u)/keyring/ssh</code> explicitly. You don't need to do anything unless SSH fails; <code>TESTBOX-ACCESS.md</code> §0 has the details.
# '''The testbox needs a Python 3.7 or newer with pyserial''' for the probe and the console tools (check with <code><PY> -c 'import sys, serial; print(sys.version)'</code>). Where the default <code>python3</code> is older, the tools use a newer one (example: on tb105 <code>python3</code> is 3.6, so <code>python3.8</code> is used). If a box does not mount the NFS lab home, the probe is copied to the box's <code>/tmp/ckprobe/</code> and run from there.
# '''The box's deployed <code>.setup</code> must be reachable''' at <code>/home/st-art/st-art/configs/<TB>.setup</code>, unless the box has none yet (the tools then say "no template"). Example: after a tb470 reboot <code>/nfsHome</code> may be unmounted, and then its <code>.setup</code> looks missing even though the file is intact. Re-mounting needs root (<code>sudo mount /nfsHome</code>), so you do it.
# '''The deployed <code>.setup</code> must describe the bench as it is now.''' A framework run binds that file. If units, cabling or console speeds have changed since the last <code>apply</code>, the probe reports MISMATCH, and every case that depends on what moved waits until you <code>apply</code>. Example, IE520 on tb470, 6 October 2026: bootloader 9.2.0 moved the stack's consoles from 115200 to 9600 baud. A <code>.setup</code> still declaring 115200 makes the consoles look dead to the framework. If you know the bench changed, run <code>/orient-dt</code> or the probe and decide on <code>apply</code> before you start a campaign.
# '''Your dev host's default box (optional).''' A dev host's default box comes from <code>bench-setup/default-boxes</code>: one line per host, <code><hostname> <tbNNN></code> (hostname case-insensitive). Add your own host's line once; never edit or add another user's line. With no line, there is no default: name the box, or give <code>bench_probe.py</code> <code>--box tbNNN</code> (or set <code>$BENCH_BOX</code>). <code>/test-mode</code> always asks for the box and offers the one it finds. <code>/orient-dt</code> and <code>/wrap-dt</code> pick the box in this order:
#* the box you name;
#* else the last test bench run recorded under your <code>user@host</code>;
#* else your host's <code>default-boxes</code> line;
#* else '''SKIPPED''' (no box touched).

== Invoking it ==

<pre>
/test-mode T24032 T12067                 # case IDs
/test-mode 33235, "Fixed port speed"     # IDs, titles, or a mix
/test-mode --resume                      # carry on with the newest campaign queue
/test-mode --resume <TB>/<FAMILY>/CAMPAIGN-QUEUE-<STAMP>.md   # a specific queue
</pre>

With neither a list nor <code>--resume</code>, it asks for the list and stops.

To see more of what the tester is doing, ask the sentinel to switch to verbose at any time. See [[#Normal and verbose modes]].

== The setup questions ==

The sentinel asks these together, before any box is touched. Each one takes free text, and the sentinel offers the obvious options.

{| class="wikitable"
! Question !! What to give !! Why it matters
|-
| '''Testbox''' || <code>tbNNN</code>. It offers the box from your last recorded test bench run or your host's <code>default-boxes</code> line, if there is one, and always "Other". It never preselects a box it did not find that way. || Selects the box's files (bench state, the table of unit names and PDU outlets, the deployed <code>.setup</code>) and where the output goes.
|-
| '''U interfaces''' || The <code>/dev/uN</code> consoles this session uses, and what is on each if you know (e.g. <code>u2,u4,u5 = stack; u3 = DUT2</code>) || '''Only these are ever probed or opened.''' Everything else on the box is someone else's.
|-
| '''PDU''' || The PDU's IP and the outlet for each console (e.g. <code>u2=6, u3=8</code>), or "no PDU / do not power-cycle" || Asked before the probe because the probe writes it into the <code>.setup</code>'s power section. With no PDU, the framework's post-failure power cycle silently does nothing, so that answer is recorded too.
|-
| '''Session constraints''' || e.g. "shared box: read-only probe, log out of consoles", a time window, devices or cases not to touch, the box's lab segment (return path), who else uses it || Constraints can tighten the standing orders, never loosen anything they mark '''always'''.
|}

A '''multi-hour''' question follows if the run is long (more than a handful of cases, or reloads, failovers or long observation windows) and you are in the VS Code editor; see [[#Running long campaigns: use tmux]].

All the answers go into a '''Session facts''' block at the top of the campaign's queue file, word for word and dated. Its first line is <code>Test Engineer: <whoami>@<hostname></code>; that is how <code>/orient-dt</code>, <code>/wrap-dt</code> and <code>/create-logs</code> later find "your last test bench run". On <code>--resume</code> the sentinel asks only for facts the queue lacks, plus a one-line "still the same?" confirmation.

== What happens, step by step ==

{| class="wikitable"
! # !! Step !! Who !! What you see
|-
| 1 || '''Setup questions''' || Sentinel → you || The questions above. It also reads <code>STANDING-ORDERS.md</code> (the standing answers), <code>TESTBOX-ACCESS.md</code>, the general traps in <code>/orient-dt</code>, and the DUT family's <code>platforms/<FAMILY>.md</code>. If there is no platform file for the family, the triage report says so.
|-
| 2 || '''Multi-hour?''' || Sentinel → you || If yes and you are in the VS Code editor, it explains the risk and offers to stop so you can restart in <code>tmux</code>.
|-
| 3 || '''Write the queue''' || Sentinel || <code><TB>/<FAMILY>/CAMPAIGN-QUEUE-<STAMP>.md</code>: your session facts, a Queue table (one row per group, with state and notes), an empty Results table and an Issues list. It is committed before anything runs, because '''it is the resume point'''.
|-
| 4 || '''Occupancy check''' || Sentinel (read-only ssh, '''no console opened''') || '''CLEAR''': it carries on. '''FOUND''': it stops and shows you what it found. See [[#The occupancy check]].
|-
| 5 || '''Arm the sentinel''' || Sentinel || A one-line confirmation: armed, which mode, where the live feed file is, and how to switch modes. See [[#How the sentinel works]].
|-
| 6 || '''Probe and triage''' || Tester (sub-agent, mode TRIAGE) || The tester repeats the occupancy check, then probes ''your'' consoles with ''your'' PDU facts. A '''USER-CONFLICT''' comes back to you as a question (see [[#When your facts and the bench disagree]]). A MISMATCH or NEEDS-CHECK is shown to you with its diff. Otherwise you get the triage report verbatim: '''N runnable / M blocked by topology (with the exact change that unblocks each) / K blocked by something else'''.
|-
| 7 || '''Proceed or reconfigure?''' || You || ''Proceed'': the N run, and the blocked rows are marked BLOCKED with their reason. ''Reconfigure'': you make the change (recable, destack, <code>apply</code> a new <code>.setup</code>) and say done. Triage then runs again, with a fresh check and probe. Repeat until you say proceed.
|-
| 8 || '''Run''' || Tester (one sub-agent per group, mode RUN) || For each case the tester saves and commits the <code>.cfg</code> files and working log, then sends a <code>RESULT</code> line. The sentinel adds it to the Results table and shows you '''one line''' per case, e.g. <code>T12589 FAIL -- <reason>  (3/12: 2 PASS, 1 FAIL)</code>. Otherwise it stays quiet unless something needs you.
|-
| 9 || '''Completion''' || Sentinel || The final results list and the blocked rows, then it ends with the line ''"please run /create-logs after reviewing the results for the final uploadable product."'' and stops. See [[#At the end of a campaign]].
|}

Between groups nothing runs on the bench, so that is the cheapest time to recable for a blocked group. The sentinel says so if one is pending and re-triages that group before running it. Before each dispatch it also restates any topology gap the triage found ("cases X need Y; fit Z first or accept UNSUPPORTED"), because a gap mentioned hours earlier gets buried.

== The occupancy check ==

Before anything opens a console, the box is checked for anything that holds, or could fight over, your consoles. The check sends '''nothing''' to any console, not even a carriage return. It is the probe's <code>precheck</code> command:

<pre>
ssh <TB> 'cd ~/claude/device-testing/bench-setup && <PY> bench_probe.py --box <TB> precheck --consoles 2-5'
</pre>

{| class="wikitable"
! Looks at !! How
|-
| Each of your consoles || Resolves <code>/dev/uN</code> to its <code>ttyUSB</code> device and runs <code>fuser -v</code> on it (with <code>sudo -n</code> where passwordless sudo works). Checks lock files under both names.
|-
| The whole box || Every <code>screen</code>, <code>tmux</code>, <code>minicom</code>, <code>picocom</code>-type process and every running python script, whoever owns it. For a root-owned <code>sudo minicom</code> it walks back to the person who started it.
|-
| Who is logged in || <code>w</code>, for information.
|}

* '''CLEAR''' (exit 0): the probe may run.
* '''FOUND''' (exit 5): the sentinel '''stops and returns to you''' with the list: which console, which process, which user, how long it has been up. It never kills, detaches or displaces anything. Re-run when it is clear, or narrow your consoles to the free ones.
* '''UNKNOWN counts as FOUND.''' Without passwordless sudo, a root-owned <code>sudo minicom</code> is invisible to <code>fuser</code> and looks exactly like a free console, so such a console is reported as unknown rather than free.
* '''Idle is not free.''' A minicom open for hours is still someone's console.
* An ssh failure is reported the same way, never worked around.

The tester repeats the check immediately before every probe it runs, because time has passed since the sentinel's check.

== When your facts and the bench disagree ==

The probe is given your session facts (<code>--pdu</code>, <code>--outlet uN=…</code>, and <code>--name uN=…</code> if you gave names) and uses them for that run.
* A unit that the box's facts file (<code><TB>.static</code>) does not list yet is '''appended''' with your facts.
* A recorded line is '''never rewritten'''.
* When your fact and the record or the bench disagree, the probe reports a '''USER-CONFLICT''' and exits 4. For example: you said outlet 7 for u2 but the record says 6; you gave a PDU IP that differs from the recorded one; or you gave facts for a console where no device answered.

The tester stops the triage and hands the conflicts back. The sentinel then asks you about each one, e.g. ''"The session says PDU outlet 7 for u2 (S/N …); the record says 6. Which is right?"''
* '''Your session fact is right:''' with your go-ahead, that one line of the facts file is changed, with a dated note naming you.
* '''The record is right:''' the queue's Session facts block is corrected, and you are told so.

Nothing is changed on either side without your answer. Triage then runs again.

The other probe results:
{| class="wikitable"
! Exit !! Meaning !! What happens
|-
| 0 MATCH || The bench is the deployed <code><TB>.setup</code>. || Triage, or the run, goes ahead.
|-
| 1 MISMATCH || The bench is not the template. || Triage works from what the bench ''is''. You see the diff. In a run, cases that depend on what moved do not start; the rest carry on. <code>apply</code> is your call.
|-
| 2 NEEDS-CHECK || Something could not be verified: a NIC with no carrier, a MAC not learned, a console busy or silent. || Shown to you; yours to resolve.
|-
| "no template" || The box has no deployed <code>.setup</code> yet. || The generated <code>bench-state.md</code> is the only description of the box. Writing the template (<code>apply</code>) is yours.
|}
The tester never "fixes" the bench or a record to make a check pass. MATCH is also not the same as healthy: the probe's Advisories block can still flag problems, and the tester reads it.

== Where everything is written ==

Everything a campaign produces goes in the <code>device-testing</code> repository under '''<code><TB>/<FAMILY>/</code>'''.
* <code><STAMP></code> is the campaign's start time, local, <code>YYYY-MM-DDTHHMM</code>, shared by all its groups.
* <code><id></code> is the case ID without its prefix (<code>38472</code> for AWPTCM-T38472).
* <code><dev></code> is a device's name in the box's <code>.setup</code> (e.g. <code>stk_a</code>, <code>swi_b</code>).

<pre>
<TB>/<FAMILY>/CAMPAIGN-QUEUE-<STAMP>.md               the queue and the results list: the resume point
<TB>/<FAMILY>/<group>-<STAMP>/README.md               the group's verdict table        (written by /create-logs)
<TB>/<FAMILY>/<group>-<STAMP>/<id>/<dev>.cfg          one per device, saved after setup (a deliverable)
<TB>/<FAMILY>/<group>-<STAMP>/<id>/work/run<N>.log    the tester's working log, one per run of the case
<TB>/<FAMILY>/<group>-<STAMP>/<id>/work/…             this case's own step scripts, pre/post configs, small captures
<TB>/<FAMILY>/<group>-<STAMP>/<id>/<id><suffix>.log   the final log                    (written ONLY by /create-logs)
<TB>/<FAMILY>/SESSION-HANDOVER-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md        the session handover             (written by /wrap-dt)
</pre>

Example: <code>tb470/IE520/routing-2026-10-02T0900/12589/</code>.

* '''During the campaign''' a case folder holds its <code>.cfg</code> files and <code>work/</code>. '''After <code>/create-logs</code>''' it holds exactly its one <code>.log</code> and its <code>.cfg</code> files.
* A case that was never attempted (NOT TESTED) gets no folder; the results list carries the reason.
* Raw console transcripts stay on the box (<code>/tmp/<campaign>/console-<uN>.log</code>) and are never committed.
* Reusable helpers go in the repo-root <code>tools/</code>, never in a case folder. See [[#Helper tools]].
* The rules for every one of these files are in <code>logged-output.md</code> at the repo root. That file is their only home; if this page and it ever differ, it wins.

The box's own measured state lives in <code>bench-setup/</code>:
{| class="wikitable"
! Box !! Files
|-
| any box || <code>bench-setup/<TB>/</code>: <code>bench-state.md</code>, <code><TB>.static</code>, <code><TB>.setup.current</code>, <code>captures/</code>, <code>backups/</code>
|-
| tb470 (the exception) || the same set kept flat in <code>bench-setup/</code>, where it always was
|}
The deployed template is <code>/home/st-art/st-art/configs/<TB>.setup</code> on the box.

'''Older campaigns stay as they are.''' Before 2 October 2026 logs were flat (<code><group>-<STAMP>/<case-id>.log</code>), and on tb470 before 1 October they were under <code>IE520/<group>-<date>/</code>. They are not rewritten, and <code>/create-logs</code> does not regenerate them. A case re-run in a new campaign gets a new folder and a new log.

== Verdicts and the results list ==

Every attempted case gets exactly one verdict. '''The tester grades it'''; you may re-grade it during review. The final log's name carries the verdict:

{| class="wikitable"
! Verdict !! Final log !! Meaning
|-
| PASS || <code><id>.log</code> || Ran, and every step the platform supports passed. UNSUPPORTED steps inside it do not stop a PASS. '''Only a PASS may use the plain name.'''
|-
| FAIL || <code><id>-fail.log</code> || Ran unsuccessfully: a check failed, or the platform prevented it from running.
|-
| PARTIAL || <code><id>-partial.log</code> || Was ''unable'' to run fully (a physical or other misconfiguration, a script error), and no FAIL condition was met.
|-
| UNSUPPORTED || <code><id>-unsupported.log</code> || The platform does not support what the case tests.
|-
| NOT TESTED || no folder, no log || Never attempted. The results list carries the reason.
|}

In short: a platform gap is UNSUPPORTED, a bench or script gap is PARTIAL, and a case nobody attempted is NOT TESTED. The old <code>-skip.log</code> is retired. The full definitions, in the bench owner's words, are in <code>logged-output.md</code> §1.

'''The results list''' is the <code>## Results</code> table in the campaign's queue file, kept by the sentinel. It has one row per case with the columns ''case, title, group, verdict, reason, working log, graded''. ''graded'' is <code>tester</code>, or <code>Test Engineer, re-graded from <VERDICT> on <date></code>. It is what you review, and what <code>/create-logs</code> builds from.

== How the sentinel works ==

The sentinel is '''mandatory''' for any session that runs tests (standing order, 28 September 2026). It has two jobs:
* '''Rescue:''' it notices a tester that has stalled or stopped early, and gets it going again.
* '''Channel:''' you talk to the sentinel, which is never busy with the bench, so you never wait for a tester's turn to finish. It relays your direction to the tester and the tester's questions to you.

In <code>/test-mode</code> the sentinel is the session you are typing into. '''It never opens a console''': no console bytes, no config, no device login. Its only contact with the box is the read-only occupancy check, which touches no console. Two writers on one console is the classic failure, so the sentinel only sends facts, and the tester does the work.

=== Its parts ===

{| class="wikitable"
! Part !! What it is !! Lifetime
|-
| '''Watcher''' (<code>sentinel.sh</code> under a Claude Code ''Monitor'', told your testbox) || A shell loop that wakes every 30 s and makes '''one''' SSH call to the testbox, reading only the new bytes of the console transcripts and framework logs. It never opens a console. On the dev host it also reads the sub-agents' transcripts and their background-task output. It never reads the sentinel's own transcript, which would feed its own events back to it. || A Monitor expires after 30 min. The sentinel re-arms it on every expiry. Read offsets persist, so nothing is missed or replayed across a re-arm.
|-
| '''Backstop''' (a 15-minute cron trigger in the session, at :10, :25, :40, :55) || A periodic check that wakes the sentinel even if the watcher has died, classifies the tester (healthy / needs you / stalled) and acts. || Lives in this session only: '''closing the session kills it'''.
|-
| '''Completion notifications''' || A sub-agent that finishes, or ends its turn early, notifies the session that started it. || This is the primary stall signal in the one-session shape.
|-
| '''Brief''' (filled-in template in the session scratchpad) || The sentinel's standing orders for this campaign: testbox and consoles, tester name, queue file, stand-down time, mode. || Never committed: it names live process details.
|-
| '''Stand-down time''' || A hard stop for the watcher (default: the end of your working day; the sentinel asks if you did not say). || The watcher exits when it is reached.
|}

=== Normal and verbose modes ===

{| class="wikitable"
! Mode !! What the sentinel is shown
|-
| '''normal''' (default) || Every console byte sent and received, plus the rescue alarms. The bytes come from the tester's <code>console.py</code> transcripts (<code>/tmp/*/console-*.log</code> on the box) and the framework's per-device console logs (<code>/home/st-art/pytest-create/*/*/{swi,stk}_*.log</code>).
|-
| '''verbose''' || Normal, plus the tester's narration, every command it runs and its output, its background-task output, and the framework's other logs.
|}

* '''Switch at any time''' by asking the sentinel. It writes <code>verbose</code> or <code>normal</code> to a mode file, and no re-arm is needed.
* '''Every line the watcher prints wakes the sentinel and costs tokens''', so output is capped at 40 lines per source per 30-second tick.
* The '''full verbose feed is always written''' to <code><scratchpad>/sentinel.feed</code>, whatever the mode. For a free live view, run <code>tail -f</code> on it in your own terminal. That is cheaper than running the sentinel in verbose for hours.

=== How it talks to you ===

* '''Healthy ticks are silent.''' The sentinel does not narrate progress.
* '''Each finished case is one line'''. The sentinel checks the tester's <code>RESULT</code> line against the working log, then adds it to the Results table and commits. If the log and the line disagree, or the log is missing, the row is still written, with the mismatch noted, and you are told. The sentinel does not pick a side.
* '''You can re-grade at any time''': say e.g. "12589 is a PASS". The Results row is changed, marked as re-graded by you, committed, and confirmed in one line. The tester's working log is not edited.
* When the tester needs you, the sentinel puts it under a bold '''NEEDS YOU:''' header, with a running list of everything still unanswered. It never ends its turn leaving one unacknowledged. Remote Control is disabled by company setting, so '''the session text is the only channel'''. Check back on long runs.
* Your answer is relayed as "Test Engineer's answer, relayed: …", and your direction ("stop after this case", "write the handover now") as "Test Engineer's instruction, relayed: …". The sentinel relays only what you said and never supplies an answer of its own.
* A new fact mid-campaign (another console, a corrected outlet) is written into the queue's Session facts with the time, relayed, and carried by the next probe.
* The sentinel batches its messages and adds "no reply needed". In the September 2026 campaign three of four tester stalls came straight after a sentinel message.

== What the sub-agent does ==

The tester is the '''<code>bench-runner</code>''' agent, started by the sentinel as a background sub-agent. Every dispatch carries one mode and a '''session block''': testbox, consoles, PDU, outlets, names, constraints, session directory and stamp. A dispatch without one is refused.

=== TRIAGE ===

Read-only apart from the bench probe.
* It runs the gate below, then checks every case's cabling needs against the measured topology (an offline preflight of each script).
* It reports N runnable / M blocked by topology / K blocked otherwise. Each topology block comes with the exact change that removes it (which port to cable to which, which device to add or move, which outlet to record, which unit to destack), stated so someone at the bench can do it without asking. A case is never "fitted" to the bench by weakening what it checks.
* It changes no device state and runs no case.
* '''A USER-CONFLICT stops triage''' and goes straight back to you, because names and outlets feed the <code>.setup</code> every case binds.
* A second TRIAGE message after a recable means a fresh occupancy check and probe; it never trusts the earlier capture.

=== RUN ===

One group of queue rows per dispatch. '''Before the group's first case''' it writes the group's bench setup and its exact restore recipe into the queue file and commits them, so a fresh tester can restore the bench if this one dies mid-group. Before each run it passes '''the pre-run gate''':

{| class="wikitable"
! # !! Check !! If it fails
|-
| 1 || '''Occupancy check''' on your consoles (<code>bench_probe.py precheck</code>, no console opened). || FOUND goes to you verbatim as <code>NEEDS TEST ENGINEER:</code>. It '''never displaces''' anyone. An ST-ART framework run it finds is somebody's test, not drift.
|-
| 2 || '''No console is parked''' in a root shell (left by a killed run) or in config mode. || Records the state in the working log, then exits it.
|-
| 3 || '''The box's template path resolves''' (<code>/home/st-art/st-art/configs/<TB>.setup</code> exists, or the box has no template yet; on tb470, <code>/nfsHome</code> is mounted). || Yours: it needs root.
|-
| 4 || '''The bench matches its template''', measured with your facts: <code>bench_probe.py --box <TB> run --consoles … --pdu … --outlet …</code>, read-only on a shared box. || MISMATCH or NEEDS-CHECK: that run does not start; the diff and the Advisories go to you, and the tester carries on with cases that don't depend on what moved. USER-CONFLICT: it stops and hands you the conflicts. It never "fixes" the bench or a record to make it match.
|-
| 5 || '''The <code>.setup</code> the run binds is this box's''' (or the topology pair Test Composer pre-loaded), never another box's. || Does not launch.
|-
| 6 || '''Offline preflight''' of the script against that <code>.setup</code> (a missing cable otherwise looks like a script defect). || The case is BLOCKED by topology.
|-
| 7 || '''Every device boots its baseline config''': the boot config each device reported at the pre-run capture (example: <code>flash:/tb470-bench.cfg</code> on tb470), or the one a pre-loaded topology declares. It is checked before and after the run. || Fixed within the test, or reported.
|-
| 8 || Ask-CK's server run path still carries the agreed run flags. || Launch by hand instead. The server path runs none of these gates, so the tester still does them.
|-
| 9 || '''A sentinel is watching''' (the dispatch prompt says <code>sentinel: parent</code>). || Refuses to start the first case.
|-
| 10 || '''The script's defaulting commands are valid on this platform.''' A rejected command would fail every TestCase at step 1, and the framework then power-cycles every unit after each failure. || Does not launch; reports a script defect.
|}

Then, per case:
* '''Runs the framework script''' with <code>--noupdate --nodefaultcfg</code>, always. Without them the framework's default setup does four things: it rewrites every device's boot config, strips licences, reboots everything, and tries to reload firmware from the box's <code>/tftproot</code> (example: on tb470 that is a tmpfs, so the copy hangs).
* '''Has full authority within the test''': config, <code>write</code>, boot config, <code>reload</code> / <code>reload stack-member</code>, a PDU power-cycle of a DUT, test traffic from the box's NICs, and scratch in the box's <code>/tmp</code>. That covers '''your consoles and your PDU outlets only''', within your constraints. It asks nobody. '''It restores what the case changed.'''
* '''Saves one <code><dev>.cfg</code> per device''' the case uses, after setup and before step 1. Each file is the device's running config, starting with three <code>!</code> header lines that name the device, the case and run, and the box and console. '''A stack is one device with one <code>.cfg</code>''' (the master's). A re-run overwrites them.
* '''Writes <code>work/run<N>.log</code> as it goes''': the session facts, the devices and links, every command with its prompt, the raw output that proves each step, the tools and arguments used, the before/after probe results and the teardown diff. It labels the run ''clean'' or ''confounded'', and ends with a <code>VERDICT:</code> line. A re-run starts <code>run<N+1>.log</code>. The full list is in <code>logged-output.md</code> §2.
* '''Drives consoles through <code>tools/console.py</code>''' or the tools built on it, with transcripts at the box's <code>/tmp/<run>/console-<uN>.log</code>, the path the sentinel watches. A console driven any other way is invisible to the sentinel.
* '''After the run:''' on every console it touched it sends <code>end</code> first, then <code>terminal no monitor</code>. Both <code>terminal</code> commands work only at the exec prompt, so sent in config mode they fail. On a shared box it also logs out. It then re-probes with the same facts (expects MATCH), diffs each device's running config against the pre-run capture, and stops anything it started.
* '''Commits the case folder''', then sends the sentinel <code>RESULT <id> <VERDICT> -- <one-line reason> -- <group>-<STAMP>/<id>/work/run<N>.log</code> and carries on.
* '''Never writes the final log or the group README''', and never deletes <code>work/</code>. Those are <code>/create-logs</code>, on your request.
* '''Updates its queue row''' as the state changes. It '''hands back''' when the group is done or every remaining row is BLOCKED, with verdicts, working-log paths and commit hashes. If it stops for any other reason it says exactly which row is next.

'''Not the tester's to decide''' (the <code>bench-runner</code> "Not yours to decide" list; see also <code>STANDING-ORDERS.md</code> §4):
* anything that contradicts your session facts;
* a console outside your list, or a holder the occupancy check found;
* licences (a case that needs a feature the unit lacks is UNSUPPORTED, not a licence request);
* a box you do not own or have not been given;
* applying a new <code>.setup</code>, or leaving the standing topology changed;
* root on the box (keys, sshd, routes, firewall rules, mounts, device trust);
* writes outside the three repositories;
* traffic beyond the box's own lab segment (example: tb470's is <code>10.38.215.0/24</code>; another box: what your constraints say, else it asks).

For these it records the need in the working log, sends the sentinel one line starting <code>NEEDS TEST ENGINEER:</code>, and '''carries on with the next runnable case'''. It never sits on a prompt.

== At the end of a campaign ==

{| class="wikitable"
! # !! Step !! Who !! What happens
|-
| 1 || '''Results list''' || Sentinel || When every group is DONE or BLOCKED it shows the final results list from the queue's Results table (verdict, reason, graded-by and working log for each case), the counts by verdict (NOT TESTED included), and the BLOCKED rows with the exact change each still needs. It ends with ''"please run /create-logs after reviewing the results for the final uploadable product."'' and stops. It does '''not''' run <code>/create-logs</code> or <code>/wrap-dt</code>, and it stays armed so you can still give direction.
|-
| 2 || '''Review and re-grade''' || You || Read the list, open any working log you want to check, and re-grade anything you disagree with ("12589 is a PASS"). Re-grades are recorded in the Results table, never in the working log.
|-
| 3 || '''<code>/create-logs</code>''' || You run it || Builds the final output from what is committed. Details below.
|-
| 4 || '''Attach in Zephyr''' || You || Attach each case's <code>.log</code> and <code>.cfg</code> files to the case in Zephyr (Jira). '''No tool here uploads anything.'''
|-
| 5 || '''<code>/wrap-dt</code>''' || You run it || Stands the sentinel down (watcher, cron, stray sweep) and confirms no tester is still running. Restores what the session changed, ending each console with <code>end</code> then <code>terminal no monitor</code>. Re-probes the bench on your consoles, writes the dated session handover with its Session facts, and commits. It never writes or edits a case log and never deletes <code>work/</code>. If you wrap before <code>/create-logs</code>, the handover lists, per group, how many cases still hold <code>work/</code> and the <code>/create-logs</code> command to finish them.
|}

Steps 3 and 5 can come in either order and in different sessions. <code>/create-logs</code> reminds you to run <code>/wrap-dt</code> if the session has not been wrapped yet.

=== /create-logs ===

<code>/create-logs</code> turns a reviewed campaign into the files you attach in Zephyr. It runs '''only when you ask''', never on its own and never as part of <code>/test-mode</code> or <code>/wrap-dt</code>. You can also start it by saying "create the logs" or "make the final logs".

<pre>
/create-logs                                              # this session's campaign, else your newest one
/create-logs <TB>/<FAMILY>/CAMPAIGN-QUEUE-<STAMP>.md       # a specific campaign
/create-logs <TB>/<FAMILY>/CAMPAIGN-QUEUE-<STAMP>.md 24032 # only some cases of it
</pre>

'''Where and with what.''' Run it in the sentinel session or any later session started in the repo root. '''It never touches a testbox''': no ssh, no console, no probe. It uses only what is committed: the queue's Results table, each case's <code>work/</code> folder and its <code>.cfg</code> files. With no queue file named, it takes this session's campaign if there was one, else the newest queue whose Session facts name you (<code>user@host</code>), and says which it took.

'''What it does, in order:'''
{| class="wikitable"
! # !! Step !! Detail
|-
| 1 || '''Reconcile''' || Checks every Results row against the folders, never from memory. An attempted case needs a <code>work/run<N>.log</code> whose <code>VERDICT:</code> agrees with the table, unless you re-graded it. A case that already has its final log and no <code>work/</code> is done and skipped, so running it again is safe. A case with <code>work/</code> but no Results row (still running, or never reported) is left alone and listed. NOT TESTED rows need no folder.
|-
| 2 || '''Confirm once''' || Shows the table it is about to build from (case, verdict, graded-by, working log, <code>.cfg</code> files present) and anything that did not reconcile, then asks: ''Yes, create them'' / ''Re-grade first'' / ''Not yet''. ''Re-grade first'' takes your changes into the Results table and asks again; ''Not yet'' changes nothing. '''It never re-grades on its own'''; a verdict that looks wrong to it is named in the summary for you to decide.
|-
| 3 || '''Write each final log''' || <code><id><suffix>.log</code>, from the template in <code>logged-output.md</code> §4, using the '''latest run only'''. Details below the table.
|-
| 4 || '''Check the <code>.cfg</code> files''' || Every device in the log's topology needs its <code><dev>.cfg</code>, with its three <code>!</code> header lines. A missing one is named to you; it is never invented or reconstructed.
|-
| 5 || '''Check the tools''' || Any helper the working log names that exists only in <code>work/</code> is moved into <code>tools/</code> with a <code>tools/README.md</code> entry, and you are told.
|-
| 6 || '''Check every final log''' || The name's suffix matches the Results verdict; the header is complete and ''Graded'' matches the table; the verdict block is present; every STEP has a verdict; every <code>.cfg</code> it names exists; no mention of an earlier run, another campaign, the sentinel or <code>work/</code>. A case that fails a check keeps its <code>work/</code> and is listed.
|-
| 7 || '''Write the group <code>README.md</code>''' || One line (testbox, DUT, date span) and a verdict table with every case of the group, NOT TESTED included, each linked to its log. No other prose. It is rewritten in full each time, so a later run for the same group leaves it complete.
|-
| 8 || '''Clean up and commit''' || Deletes <code>work/</code> only for cases that passed step 6, and checks that each folder now holds exactly its one <code>.log</code> and its <code>.cfg</code> files. One commit per group, <code>create-logs: <group>-<STAMP> — <n> logs (<counts by verdict>)</code>. It never pushes. The working files stay in git history.
|-
| 9 || '''Report''' || The table of final logs (case, verdict, log path, <code>.cfg</code> files); anything skipped or failing a check; any claim left out for lack of a source; any tool moved; the commit hashes; and ''"The logs and .cfg files under <TB>/<FAMILY>/<group>-<STAMP>/<id>/ are ready to attach in Zephyr."''
|}

'''What a final log contains:'''
* A header: Run, Bench, Tester, Graded, Case, Build, Configs.
* The <code>VERDICT:</code> line, with what was proven, then the verdict block:
** FAIL: <code>FAIL CONDITION:</code> (and <code>TRIED:</code> when there was more than one attempt);
** PARTIAL: <code>NOT RUN:</code> and <code>UNBLOCK:</code>;
** UNSUPPORTED: <code>NEEDS:</code> and <code>ABSENT:</code>;
** PASS: none; each UNSUPPORTED step is shown in its own STEP.
* A <code>CAVEAT:</code> saying what the run did not establish.
* TOPOLOGY AS TESTED: devices, serials, consoles, links, host NICs and tools. Together with the <code>.cfg</code> files, it is enough to rebuild the case.
* One STEP block per step: its commands with their prompts, the raw output verbatim, short notes on the lines that matter, and a closing <code>=> STEP n <VERDICT>:</code> line. STEP 0 is the baseline with the feature off, when the case changes behaviour.

'''Each run stands alone.''' A final log never mentions earlier runs, other campaigns, setup detours, infrastructure findings, conversations with the sentinel, or the teardown proof; those stay in the working log and the handover. Device output is copied verbatim from the working log. A claim it cannot source from the working log is left out and named to you instead. This is why the tester's working log errs on the side of too much.

'''A large campaign''' may be split: one background helper per group writes that group's logs, and <code>/create-logs</code> checks each one against step 6 before anything is deleted or committed.

'''A campaign from before 2 October 2026''' has no Results table; <code>/create-logs</code> says so and stops. Those logs keep their old structure.

== Helper tools ==

Reusable helpers live in the repo-root '''<code>tools/</code>''', catalogued in '''<code>tools/README.md</code>''' with how to run each one. They cover:
* console drivers and a CLI answerer;
* a CLI help probe that never executes the command;
* pre-run console checks, pollers and passive recorders;
* reload, flash-copy, TFTP-copy and Boot Menu escape helpers;
* a config differ;
* traffic senders, frame counters and pcap builders;
* protocol responders (IGMP, IPv6 ND, DHCPv6, LLDP-MED phone, Modbus).

To run them, copy the whole directory to the box's <code>/tmp/<campaign>/</code> and run from there. Console tools take <code><tty> <baud> <transcript></code> first.

The rule for the tester, and for you if you write one:
# '''Look in <code>tools/README.md</code> first.''' Use or extend what is there; do not write a second tool for the same job.
# '''Write it generic.''' Testbox, consoles, NICs, ports, VLANs and addresses are arguments, never constants. If it only works on one platform, its README entry says so.
# '''Commit it with its <code>tools/README.md</code> entry''', in the same commit as the case that first needed it.
# The working log names the tool and its exact arguments, so the run can be repeated.

Only a script that is genuinely one case's own (its ports and VLANs written in) stays in that case's <code>work/</code>, and <code>/create-logs</code> deletes it with the folder.

'''Status, 6 October 2026:''' most of the catalogue was re-run on tb470 (IE520, plus an x230 at 9600 baud) on 2 October after being generalised, and each entry records what was verified. Six protocol tools (<code>igmp</code>, <code>nsresp</code>, <code>dhc6</code>, <code>rs</code>, <code>lldpmed_phone</code>, <code>mb</code>) are still marked "not re-verified on hardware", and the first run that uses one updates its status. Two limits worth knowing:
* <code>flash_copy.py</code> is pull-only: it copies into the local unit's flash. A large push to another stack member fails on IE520.
* <code>bootmenu_escape.py</code>'s menu strings are the IE520 Boot Menu's. It reads which menu is on screen and sends only the key that backs out of it.

== Recovery: what the sentinel can and cannot rescue ==

{| class="wikitable"
! What goes wrong !! How it is noticed !! What happens !! What is lost
|-
| Tester ends its turn early ("Next: running T931" and then stops: the most common failure) || Completion notification || The sentinel compares the report with the queue file and the case folders, and continues the ''same'' sub-agent by name: what completed, the exact next row, "no reply needed". || Nothing.
|-
| Sub-agent has gone (finished, crashed, out of context) with rows left || Completion notification, or the IDLE alarm "nothing running anywhere" || A fresh RUN dispatch for the remaining rows, with the same session block. Its pre-run gate re-probes the bench first, and the group's restore recipe in the queue file says how to get back to a clean state. || The case in flight, at most; the queue and per-case commits carry the rest.
|-
| Tester waiting on something that can never fire (e.g. an SSH <code>pgrep</code> loop that matches itself; one spun for 14.6 h) || IDLE alarm after 300 s of no activity, with '''STALL SIGNATURE''' (stale wait loops on the dev host and no live job on the box) || The sentinel messages the tester with what actually completed and where to resume. || The idle time.
|-
| Tester needs you || <code>NEEDS TEST ENGINEER:</code> message || Surfaced under '''NEEDS YOU:''', and your answer relayed back. The sentinel does not nudge, because the tester has already moved on. || Nothing; only the blocked case waits.
|-
| Someone starts using one of your consoles mid-campaign || The tester's occupancy check before its next probe || It stops before that run and sends you the FOUND list. || The wait.
|-
| Watcher killed (editor or VPN drop, 30-min expiry) || Expiry notification, or the 15-minute cron finds no watcher this session armed || Re-armed by the arming procedure: '''sweep and kill stray watchers first''', clear the heartbeat, arm. Offsets persist, so nothing is replayed or missed. || Nothing.
|-
| Orphaned watcher keeping the heartbeat fresh while its output goes nowhere || A heartbeat is trusted only if ''this'' session armed the watcher || Treated as dead: swept and re-armed. || Nothing.
|-
| Usage window runs out mid-campaign || The cron fires after the window refreshes || Continues or re-dispatches from the first row not DONE / BLOCKED. || The wait.
|-
| '''The session's process dies''' (window closed, editor reload, xrdp/VPN drop takes the editor) || Nothing in-session: the sentinel, its cron and the sub-agent all die together || '''You''' start a session in the repo root and run <code>/test-mode --resume</code>. Details below the table. || The case in flight.
|}

On <code>--resume</code> after the session died, the new session:
# reads the queue file and its session facts, and confirms them with you;
# reconciles the Results table with the case folders: a committed working log that ends in a <code>VERDICT:</code> line but has no Results row gets its row;
# runs the occupancy check;
# says which row is next;
# re-arms the sentinel and continues.

The sentinel '''cannot''' fix the bench, take a bench-level decision for you, or lift a mechanical block: the no-stray-scripts hook, the auto-mode safety classifier and the company <code>git push</code> denial do not change because a message was relayed. Those come back to you to do yourself.

=== Running long campaigns: use tmux ===

In the one-session shape the tester lives inside the session's process, so if that process dies the whole campaign stops until someone resumes it.
* A VS Code window is exposed to editor reloads and connection drops: in September 2026 a VPN drop killed an editor-attached watcher.
* A bare terminal is not safer: closing it sends SIGHUP.
* A terminal inside <code>tmux</code> (or <code>screen</code>) survives a closed window or a dropped connection:
<pre>
tmux new -s test-mode
cd <lab home>/claude/device-testing
claude
/test-mode <cases>          # re-attach later with:  tmux attach -t test-mode
</pre>
For a tester that must outlive its sentinel, the older '''two-session shape''' is still supported: one session runs the cases, a second watches it as a peer (<code>/orient-dt</code> §10).

== Shared testboxes ==

Most testboxes are shared: ST-ART framework runs, people on minicom, and other Claude sessions all use them. Here is how each situation is handled.

=== Someone holds a console (minicom, another script, another session) ===
* The occupancy check finds it before any console is opened, and the sentinel stops and tells you. The tester's own gate catches anything that starts later. Neither ever logs in on top of someone.
* If a console somehow reads busy during the probe anyway, the probe skips it and reports '''NEEDS-CHECK''' rather than MATCH, so no run that needs it starts.
* Say "shared box" in your constraints. The probe then runs read-only: logins and <code>show</code> commands only, no LLDP switch-on, and no MAC-learning pings out of the host NICs. (Without it, the probe switches <code>lldp run</code> on where a device has it off and leaves it on in the running config.) The tester logs out of every console it opened, because the probe otherwise leaves consoles logged in as manager.
* On a box you do not own, ask its users before probing, even when the occupancy check is CLEAR. The check shows who has a console open ''now'', not who owns the bench.

=== An ST-ART framework run is in progress ===
* Its traces are a stack hostname like <code>stk_a_<test>_<run></code> and <code>[SCRIPT]</code> lines in the device log. That is someone's test, not drift; nothing should "restore" it.
* A framework run is a python script, so the occupancy check reports it. Between steps it may hold no console and look idle: check the time of the last <code>[SCRIPT]</code> line before sending traffic, because two runs on one bench corrupt each other's results.

=== Another Claude session on the same bench ===
* '''Run one campaign per set of consoles at a time.''' Two testers configuring the same devices collide, and nothing in the tooling arbitrates between them. Sessions on ''different'' consoles of a box are fine, as long as their cases do not share devices or cabling.
* The sentinel's console feed reads '''every''' console transcript under the box's <code>/tmp/*/</code> and the framework run directories, so another session's console traffic shows up in your feed.
* The IDLE alarm counts '''any''' <code>python3</code> or <code>tcpdump</code> on the box as a live job, so another user's job can mask a stalled tester. Completion notifications are unaffected and remain the primary signal.

=== Two /test-mode sessions on the same dev host ===
* '''Avoid it for now.''' The arming procedure kills ''every'' <code>sentinel.sh</code> process it finds on the host before arming its own. So one session's re-arm (every 30 min, and on each cron backstop that finds no watcher) kills the other session's watcher, and each keeps killing the other's.
* Each session's own completion notifications still work, but stall detection and the console feed flip between them.

== Notes ==

* '''Standing orders apply to every Test Engineer.''' <code>STANDING-ORDERS.md</code> holds the bench owner's standing answers: device authority within a test, the triage report shape, the between-TestCase rule, and what always stays yours. Your session constraints can tighten them for a session, and a campaign's queue file can add overrides for that campaign; neither can loosen anything marked '''always'''. The logging rules are in <code>logged-output.md</code>.
* '''Time and power cycles.''' After any TestCase that ends FAIL, UNSUPPORTED or ERROR, the framework power-cycles every device the <code>.setup</code> lists (example: about 4 minutes for tb470's six units). This is accepted by design; nothing works around it. A script that fails every case at the same defaulting step is stopped instead, after two consecutive failures. Budget generously for reloads and failovers. Example, IE520: copying a release into SPI flash takes about 12 minutes for 41 MB, and the unit answers nothing meanwhile. It looks crashed, but never power-cycle it then.
* '''Those power cycles show up as <code>Unexpected System reboot</code>''' in every unit's <code>show reboot history</code>, one entry per failed case, all at the same minute. Match them against the run's <code>Power cycle … completed</code> lines before treating any as a real unexplained reboot. The IE520 and x230 log reboot history in UTC.
* '''Bench setup changes once per TestSet, not between its cases.''' Cabling, aggregator changes, VLAN isolation and boot pointers are set before the TestSet and restored after it. A case that needs a different physical setup belongs in a different group.
* '''Configs are kept tidy between unrelated cases.''' Each case's additions are removed, and the removal is checked by diffing the running config against the pre-case copy; that proof stays in the working log. Nothing is written to startup config unless the case requires it.
* '''Legacy (hand-written) suites have three extra traps''' that generated scripts do not. All three were seen with T24032 on tb470, 2 October 2026:
** their TestSet powers '''off''' every device it did not initialise, so partner units go dark: switch the outlets back on and re-probe before the next case;
** they hard-code test VLAN IDs and delete them in tear-down: check them against the bench's VLANs before launch, and remap a collision in the staged copy (your call), never on the bench;
** the framework console wraps at 80 columns, so a one-line <code>show log</code> match can miss a long line: read the raw device log before grading such a step FAIL.
* '''The probe is the bench's source of truth.''' The box's <code>bench-state.md</code> is generated by <code>bench_probe.py run</code> and never hand-edited. Neither is the <code>.setup</code> on the box: <code>apply</code> writes it, and running <code>apply</code> is your call. The names-and-outlets file (<code><TB>.static</code>) is yours: the probe only appends new units to it.
* '''History is in git, not in the output.''' Every run of a case keeps its own <code>work/run<N>.log</code> until <code>/create-logs</code>; the final log describes the latest run only, and the <code>.cfg</code> files are the latest run's. Earlier runs and the deleted <code>work/</code> remain in git history.
* '''Nothing is pushed.''' Every commit is reported as "committed, NOT pushed". You push.
* '''Skill and agent changes need a new session.''' The skills and <code>bench-runner</code>'s definition are read when a session starts; an edit takes effect in the next session.
* '''Framework run directories under <code>/tmp/ck*/</code> are not watched''' by the default sentinel feed (it watches <code>/home/st-art/pytest-create/</code>). A tester that runs there needs an extra Monitor on its <code>run.stdout</code>.
* '''A rejected or interrupted tool call can still be running on the box''' and holding a console or changing config. Rejecting a call stops Claude reading the output, not the remote command. The tester checks <code>ps</code> and the consoles after any interrupt, before claiming nothing changed.
* '''Never send <code><command> ?</code> with a trailing Enter''' through a console driver: if <code><cr></code> is a valid completion, the command executes. <code>tools/qmark.py</code> asks for help without executing anything.
* '''<code>terminal monitor</code> and <code>terminal no monitor</code> work only at the exec prompt''', and <code>terminal monitor</code> does not toggle. Sent in config mode they fail (<code>Command [terminal no monitor] failed</code> in the device log). The console tools handle this; a hand-driven console needs <code>end</code> first.
* '''Platform limits produce UNSUPPORTED, not FAIL.''' Triage says up front which cases they touch. Example, IE520: no SD card slot, no battery-backed RAM, no SSH or telnet (console only), and no MDI/MDI-X polarity. Each product family's platform facts are in <code>platforms/<FAMILY>.md</code> (for example <code>platforms/IE520.md</code>), which <code>/test-mode</code>, <code>/orient-dt</code> and the tester read. A product with no file yet is worked from the general traps.

** <code>.claude/agents/bench-runner.agent.md</code>: the tester and its gate.
** <code>tools/README.md</code>: the catalogue of reusable helpers.
** <code>STANDING-ORDERS.md</code>: the standing orders every Test Engineer works under.

** <code>bench-setup/bench_probe.py</code>: <code>precheck</code>, <code>run</code> (with <code>--box</code> and the session-fact options), <code>apply</code>.

** <code>.claude/skills/wrap-dt/SKILL.md</code>: ending a session.
